text:
alex: quick update — ran a RoPE window-eviction experiment on mixtral / qwen to stress KV cache under longctx workloads. tried YARN + finite-window eviction, and a linear-decay fallback. initial results look noisy but interesting.

sam: can you paste the perf numbers? latency/throughput and any token-cost changes?

alex: baseline (no-evict): p50=42ms, p95=105ms, tokens/s=860
alex: yarn+evict(32k window) p50=48ms, p95=120ms, tokens/s=820, cache hit down ~6%

rita: ran profiler on the yarn run — kernel switch frequency went up, lots of small matmuls due to fragmented KV segments. flame graph shows 18% more kernel dispatch overhead.

infra-bot: deploy 2024-06-30T12:21:00 by luis — applied patch kernel-routing v2.1 to test nodes.

luis: thinking: kernel-selection threshold currently checks seq_len only. propose adding a 'kv_density' signal (fragmentation ratio) and prefer fused-kernel when density < 0.6 to avoid dispatch churn.

kai: note: mixtral shows a small perplexity bump on longctx (>64k) with yarn eviction — +0.28 ppl on wikitext-103 slices. not huge but consistent.

rita: we should set per-model safe ranges: for mixtral limit yarn-evict window to 32k and enable linear-rot fallback beyond that. for qwen we can be more aggressive.

sam: repro steps? I want to run locally with cpu-profiler + kv-trace.

alex: repro snippet:
`````
RUNTIME_PROFILE=1 KV_TRACE=1 ./bin/serve --model mixtral-8b --rope-mode yarn --rope-window 32768 --evict-strategy finite
`````
logs:
`````
[INFO] kv_hits: 0.82 kv_frag: 0.43 kernel_switches: 14/s p95:120ms
`````

luis: pseudocode for heuristic:
`````
if seq_len > 8192 and kv_frag < 0.6:
  use fused_kernel
elif kv_frag >= 0.6 and rope_mode == 'yarn':
  prefer linear_fallback
else:
  default_kernel
`````

kai: runs to do: 100 eval slices longctx, measure ppl and mt50 latency. guard: if ppl delta > 0.5 -> rollback.

rita: i'll queue the eval and add telemetry for 'kv_frag' + 'kernel_dispatch_rate' to the console. also adding regression alert rule.

sam: thanks — tag me when you have the eval results. :thumbsup:

alex: ack, will follow up with a short writeup and per-model config suggestions.
